title: Identity: the JIT user path reads the IdP locale claim into the user language preference (hosted environments follow the cloud account language)
body:
Filing gate ②: the framework half the maintainer ruled on objectstack-ai/cloud#3125 (batch #387 item 1, column 现在立 card 5: 「用户语言偏好随云账号进入每个环境」, platform first). Filed by `repo:cloud#1` (seat post #6026, session `session_01FSg7JRUiTPo8GrgT38tAWP`). ⛔ Not a claim.

**Reader who acts:** the objectstack lane. The cloud half (the control plane's OIDC provider emits `locale`) is objectstack-ai/cloud#3159, which is `Blocked-by:` this one.

## Wanted
- When the environment creates or refreshes a user just-in-time from an external IdP sign-in (the cloud as IdP on hosted environments, or any OIDC IdP), it reads the standard OIDC `locale` claim (BCP 47) into the user's language preference.
- On first creation, the claim sets the preference.
- On a later sign-in, the claim updates it only while the user has not set a preference in the environment itself; a local choice wins.
- An unknown or unsupported locale falls back to the deployment default, closed against the supported locale list.

## Acceptance
- A JIT sign-in with `locale: "zh-CN"` creates a user whose console is zh-CN.
- A later sign-in with `locale: "en"` after the user picked ja locally keeps ja.
- An unsupported `locale` falls back to the default.
